subject: IRT parametrization with multidimensional simple structure model

messages.subject: IRT parametrization with multidimensional simple structure model
parts:
Hi Phil,

because I need to link parameters from two multidimensional calibrations in two different groups, I want to use the plink package. The plink package does multidimensional linking, but requires IRT parametrization rather than the intercept/slope form from the mirt package.

The IRTpars argument does not work for multidimensional models, but because I am working with a complete simple structure model (although the traits are allowed to correlate), can I simply apply the b = -d/a formula? The values I obtain then seem to be correct, i.e. in the range of what we would expect.

Another option would be to run a multiple group with some anchors to put the parameters on the same scale, but my model is huge so runtime will be long. If I do so, I will need to freely estimate the means and covariances in the focal group am I correct?

Thank you, best

Dirk

because I need to link parameters from two multidimensional calibrations in two different groups, I want to use the plink package. The plink package does multidimensional linking, but requires IRT parametrization rather than the intercept/slope form from the mirt package.

The IRTpars argument does not work for multidimensional models, but because I am working with a complete simple structure model (although the traits are allowed to correlate), can I simply apply the b = -d/a formula? The values I obtain then seem to be correct, i.e. in the range of what we would expect.

Another option would be to run a multiple group with some anchors to put the parameters on the same scale, but my model is huge so runtime will be long. If I do so, I will need to freely estimate the means and covariances in the focal group am I correct?

Also correct. plink will make the assumption that all the items are theoretical anchors, in some sense, so pros and cons as to whether that is a good thing or not. I personally find the multiple-group approach more theoretically superior rather than assuming every item has no DIF and linking that way, even if that means a reduction in power. HTH.

Phil
 

Thank you, best
